## Claims
- [source-backed] The basic ideal is \(J_v=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\); Grassmannian cohomology is \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) with Schur classes indexed by partitions in \((n-r)^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 197-218]
- [source-backed] For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and the lower-adjoined Schur family generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- [source-backed] In \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), multiplication is truncated Littlewood–Richardson multiplication over partitions in \(q^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-269]
- [proved] For the new specialization
  \[
  (i,j,p,c)=(2,3,3,2),\quad q=i+p=5,\quad r=j+c=5,
  \]
  hence \(n=r+q=10\), \(t=r-j+1=3\), \(s=i+t-1=4\), and \(v=v_{5,4,3,10}\) is admissible.
- [proved] With \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,5}\), the exact Schur-basis interval ideal is
  \[
  J=J_v=\bigoplus_{\substack{(2,2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(5,5,5,5,5)}}\mathbb Z\,\bar s_\lambda .
  \]
- [proved] For this specialization,
  \[
  A_+=(\bar h_1,\bar h_2,\bar h_3,\bar h_4,\bar h_5).
  \]
- [proved] In every degree \(d\), the complete lattice \((A_+J)_d\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of precisely the Pieri rows
  \[
  \bar h_t\bar s_\lambda
  =\sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq\mu\subseteq5^5\\
                   \mu/\lambda\ {\rm horizontal}\ t\text{-strip}}}\bar s_\mu ,
  \quad
  1\le t\le5,\quad
  (2,2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^5,\quad |\lambda|=d-t.
  \]

## Strategy
Here \(v=v_{5,4,3,10}\) has one-line notation
\[
v=1,2,5,6,7,3,4,8,9,10.
\]
Its Grassmannian partition at descent \(r=5\) is
\[
\bigl(v(5)-5,v(4)-4,v(3)-3,v(2)-2,v(1)-1\bigr)=(2,2,2,0,0).
\]
For Grassmannian permutations, Bruhat order is partition containment. Therefore the Grassmannian classes in \(J_v\) are exactly those indexed by
\[
\mathcal I=\{\lambda:5\ge\lambda _1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda _5\ge0,\ 
\lambda _1,\lambda _2,\lambda _3\ge2\},
\]
which proves the displayed interval basis. Littlewood–Richardson containment shows this span is an ideal.

Write \(h_t=s_{(t)}\). Jacobi–Trudi gives \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\). In \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,5}\), \(\bar h_t=0\) for \(t>5\), since \((t)\nsubseteq5^5\). Thus \(A\) is generated by \(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5\). Its unit is \(\bar s_\varnothing=1\), so every positive-degree polynomial has zero constant term and lies in \((\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5)\); the reverse containment is immediate. Hence
\[
A_+=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5).
\]

Consequently
\[
A_+J=\sum_{t=1}^{5}\bar h_tJ,
\qquad
(A_+J)_d=\sum_{t=1}^{5}\bar h_tJ_{d-t}.
\]
For each \(\lambda\in\mathcal I\), the Littlewood–Richardson tableau argument with content \((t)\) gives the Pieri formula above: the coefficient is \(1\) exactly for horizontal \(t\)-strips and \(0\) otherwise. Thus the listed rows span exactly \((A_+J)_d\), not merely a sublattice.

Boundary conventions are explicit: \(\mathcal I_e=\varnothing\) for \(e<6\) or \(e>25\); no row occurs when \(\mathcal I_{d-t}=\varnothing\). A listed row with no permitted \(\mu\subseteq5^5\) is the zero row and does not change the lattice. For \(d<6\) and \(d>25\), both \(J_d\) and \((A_+J)_d\) vanish.

## Gaps
None for this structural certificate. It does not compute Smith data or assert a parent minimality theorem.
